item.title: Documents Released by House Panel Show AI Chip Approvals
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, EqualAI President Miriam Vogel says Anthropic’s IPO puts frontier AI labs under greater scrutiny from investors and regulators, as pressure builds in Washington for clearer guardrails around the technology. Nicholas Burns, who served as US Ambassador to China under President Biden and previously as US Ambassador to NATO, says President Trump’s trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin sent the wrong message to US allies, while warning that tensions over Nvidia and chip exports could further strain relations with Beijing. Republican Representative Marlin Stutzman of Indiana criticized GOP lawmakers for missing votes as the party races to finish its agenda before losing the House majority, telling absent colleagues to “get back to work.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Spain’s Sánchez Struggles in Debate Against Main Rival Feijóo
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez sought to brush off attacks from opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo in an electoral debate Thursday by apologising for corruption in his government and for two large train accidents.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Basteiro

item.title: Rep. Stutzman: GOP Must Finish Strong in Lame Duck
item.description: Republican Representative Marlin Stutzman of Indiana criticized GOP lawmakers for missing votes as the party races to finish its agenda before losing the House majority, telling absent colleagues to “get back to work.” He also pointed to unfinished business on spending, defense, permitting and the debt ceiling. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fmr. Amb. Criticizes Trump-Xi-Putin Summit Optics
item.description: Nicholas Burns, who served as US Ambassador to China under President Biden and previously as US Ambassador to NATO, says President Trump’s trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin sent the wrong message to US allies, while warning that tensions over Nvidia and chip exports could further strain relations with Beijing. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Anthropic IPO
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
Anthropic shares pared earlier gains to trade 17% above their IPO price after the artificial intelligence lab’s blockbuster $107.3 billion debut broke SpaceX’s record for the biggest-ever offering. The shares were changing hands at $96.75 each at 1:29 p.m. on Thursday in New York, after an opening surge that took it far above the IPO price of $83. The current price gives Anthropic a fully diluted market value of about $1.8 trillion, making it one of the 10 biggest public companies in the world by market cap, rivaling SpaceX and briefly challenging Amazon.com Inc. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Vogel: Anthropic IPO Brings New Scrutiny to AI
item.description: EqualAI President Miriam Vogel says Anthropic’s IPO puts frontier AI labs under greater scrutiny from investors and regulators, as pressure builds in Washington for clearer guardrails around the technology. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Makes Trading Debut
item.description: Anthropic trading opened up Thursday with shares trading well above their IPO price after the company’s $107.3 billion debut, which broke SpaceX’s record for the biggest-ever offering. On this special two-hour edition of Bloomberg Businessweek, we hear from a panel of Bloomberg experts including Senior IPO Reporter Bailey Lipschultz, Deals Reporter Ryan Gould, Head of Global Tech Research Mandeep Singh, Bloomberg Tech Host Ed Ludlow, and AI Editor Seth Fiegerman. We also hear from early Anthropic investors Sameer Dholakia of Bessemer Venture Partners and Sebastian Duesterhoeft of Lightspeed Venture Partners. Plus, Threadneedle Founder Ann Berry on why she is investing in Anthropic and plans to hold shares long-term. All on the latest episode of "Bloomberg Businessweek Daily." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wright Is Confident Congress Will Pass Energy Permitting Reform
item.description: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said he expects Congress will pass a sweeping bill to overhaul the process for approving large infrastructure projects, saying it’s the Trump administration’s “signature effort” to spur energy investment.
item.dc:creator: Emma Sanchez

item.title: Trump’s Warm Embrace of Xi and Putin Showcases His Strongman Ties
item.description: The display of strength comes as all three leaders face significant pressures.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: Trump’s Camaraderie With Xi and Putin Draws Pushback at Home
item.description: On his two-day trip to China this week, President Donald Trump glad-handed and exchanged hugs with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in an effort to flex his power after his Republican Party suffered a midterm election blowout at home.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian and Jeff Mason

item.title: Australia’s Leader to Navigate Trade, Security in Talks With Xi
item.description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will aim to navigate delicate security and trade issues when he meets Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday, seeking to ease access for commodities to its biggest export partner.
item.dc:creator: James Mayger

item.title: Europe Won't Go Back to Buying Russian Energy, Says Secretary Wright
item.description: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright speaks with Bloomberg's Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz from Warsaw. Wright says Russia and China are "absolutely very significant competitors of ours." He says in many areas, they are outright adversaries. Wright says Europe won't go back to buying Russian energy. He also talks about the flow of oil around the world, sanctions, and need for more nuclear energy in the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump, Xi, Putin's Trilateral Evokes Images of Yalta and Beyond
item.description: The trilateral meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin was billed as an opportunity for global cooperation — while raising fears that the leaders of the three largest nuclear powers are carving up spheres of influence. Even if the summit was light on concrete outcomes, the images of the leaders of the US, China and Russia at an unprecedented summit is likely to live on in history. Elizabeth Economy, Stanford Professor and Hargrove Senior Fellow, discusses the trilateral meeting and its outcomes. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Guyana’s Ali Says Border Stance Unchanged After US Overture
item.description: Guyana President Irfaan Ali said there has been “absolutely no change” in his country’s position on its border dispute with Venezuela and that both countries will have to accept an eventual ruling by the International Court of Justice.
item.dc:creator: Denis Chabrol

item.title: Trump Calls Skeptical Allies to Sell View That Putin Wants Peace
item.description: US President Donald Trump offered a triumphant assessment of his conversation with Vladimir Putin in a surprise phone call to European leaders gathered in Berlin, arguing the Russian leader wants to end the war.
item.dc:creator: Arne Delfs, Ott Tammik, Samy Adghirni and Andra Timu

item.title: Dutch, Austrian Embassies Damaged in Kyiv Projectile Strike
item.description: The Dutch and Austrian embassies in central Kyiv were damaged when projectiles from a Russian airstrike hit nearby on Thursday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Van Oosterom, Olesia Safronova and Marton Eder

item.title: Historic Trump-Xi-Putin Summit Fails to Deliver on Substance
item.description: It was a sitdown that had officials in Europe, Asia and other parts of the globe imagining the worst: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin bargaining over the likes of Ukraine and Taiwan as they carved the world into spheres of influence.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Choong Wilkins and Alan Crawford

item.title: Takaichi Walks Tightrope With Russia, China on Asia Trip
item.description: Sanae Takaichi’s trip to China for an international summit alongside rivals Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin went better than expected. Now, the question is whether she can break the diplomatic deadlock with them.
item.dc:creator: Alastair Gale and Sakura Murakami

item.title: This Is The Problem With AI's Most Bullish Chart
item.description: It has been a historic week for AI: The Anthropic IPO and the ongoing situation at Nvidia headline a head-spinning time for the industry. Despite Nvidia's earnings outlook looking good, and despite the scale of the Anthropic IPO there are so many open questions about the state of the industry right now. On today's two-part episode, first we speak with Stanley Lee, the chief product officer at Liquid Compute, and he explains why Wall Street and Silicon Valley seem to be talking past each other, and what fragilities are emerging in the credit market for GPUs. All those charts that show rising GPU rental rates, Lee tells us, might not be as industry-bullish as they first appear. Then, we turn to Paul Kedrosky, a managing partner at SK Ventures, and we discuss why “number goes up and to the right” does not necessarily prove the viability of the capex involved in the AI buildout and if Nvidia will remain the central bank for AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Xi Embraces Trump as China’s Best Option to Contain Chip Row
item.description: Xi Jinping showed Donald Trump extraordinary hospitality during their third summit of the year. For Beijing, that bonhomie might be its best strategy for stopping a spiraling chip battle with its main rival.
item.dc:creator: Nectar Gan and Annmarie Hordern
